content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions possible) 2 3 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). 4 5 Server 6 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 7 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 12 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 13 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 14 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 15 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 16 17 API 18 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 19 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 20 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 21 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 22 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 23 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 24 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 25 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 26 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 27 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 28 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 29 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 30 31 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 32 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 33 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 34 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 35 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 36 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 37 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 38 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 39 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 40 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 41 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 42 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 43 44 Page 45 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 46 - The page loads the script with a `

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. content.text:
The server conforms to the spec in every area you listed, and I found no defect. Nothing in the code blocks a pass. The only gaps are small code-quality points, plus coverage that can't be measured as set up. I didn't re-run the 191 passing tests beyond the coverage run.

**Spec conformance**
- **Startup:** `server.mjs:307-317` checks PORT, then the data file, then listens. Bad PORT, bad data file and bind failures each write one line to stderr and exit 1. The only stdout write is the `listening on` line, which uses the actually bound port.
- **Data file:** `parseState` and `isStoredBooking` (`server.mjs:78-104`) are strict. They reject a BOM (`ignoreBOM: true` keeps it, so JSON.parse fails), invalid UTF-8, extra keys, duplicate ids, an id at or above `nextId`, untrimmed titles and overlapping bookings. Only ENOENT is treated as "no bookings yet".
- **Saving:** `saveState` writes a temp file then renames it, and cleans up on failure. In `createBooking` and `deleteBooking` the state is replaced only after the save succeeds, so a failed save changes nothing and the next id stays the same. The reply is 500 `internal error` and the server keeps running.
- **Concurrency:** each request is handled in one synchronous step once its body is fully read, so requests run one at a time.
- **Body draining:** the body is read in full, then 415 is checked before 413. The size counts the bytes actually received.
- **Routing:** `route` splits at the first `?` and matches the raw path. The DELETE route applies to any non-empty id without a `/`, which gives 405 for `GET /api/bookings/abc`. Other unknown paths get 404.
- **Replies:** 204 is sent with no body, JSON replies carry the right content type, and the pages are read fresh on each request. Uncaught handler errors become 500 through the `respond` catch.

## Findings
- Structure: `server.mjs` holds validation, persistence, routing and startup in 319 lines. That is within limits, but splitting validation and storage into modules would improve cohesion.
- Structure: `ctx.state` is reassigned at `server.mjs:226` and `:239`. The bookings themselves are never mutated, and this is the single state holder, so I don't count it as a breach.
- Errors: `server.mjs:128-134` report any read failure as `cannot read data file`. That is what the spec asks for, but the error code is dropped, so a permissions problem and a corrupt file look the same.
- Tests: 191 tests cover the spec well, including rule order and the draining, save-failure and concurrency cases. The 80% coverage figure can't be measured. The server runs in a child process, so `--experimental-test-coverage` reports only 48% for `server.mjs`. The count would be higher in practice.
- Size: `test/server.test.mjs` is 739 lines, under the 800 maximum but near it.
- Leftovers: none. There is no `console.log` and no TODO.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 8 — clear small functions with a pure core; one 319-line file mixes validation, persistence and routing, and `ctx.state` is reassigned
naming: 9 — descriptive names throughout
duplication: 9 — validators are shared by the POST path and the startup check
size: 8 — server is 319 lines and every function is under 50, but the test file is 739 lines, close to the 800 maximum
errors: 9 — err.code is checked only for ENOENT and listen errors, saves are atomic, handler errors give 500 and the server survives; the catches that return null or exit 1 are intentional
tests: 8 — 191 tests with wrong-implementation traps; in-process coverage can't be measured because the server runs as a child process
security: 9 — no injection, input is validated at the boundary, errors leak nothing, path matching is raw
leftovers: 10 — clean
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/server.mjs:122-138 optional: move validation and storage into their own modules to make coverage measurable and raise cohesion.
- /root/bench-runs/h4-a87b97bc/test/server.test.mjs:1 optional: keep the file under 800 lines by splitting it by area (startup, routing, booking rules) if it grows.
